text.p: The Turkish lira fell to 89,670 per dollar on Monday from 89,260 at Friday's close, due to the central bank's higher dollar rate for banks' forex transfers.

The Turkish central bank raised its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers to 89,500 lira at the opening from 89,125 at Friday's close. Later in the day, the rate was further raised to 89,550.

The central bank injected a total of 55.85 trillion lira. It sold 15.85 trillion lira at a seven-day repo auction at an average annual rate of 71.98 percent and lent banks 40 trillion lira overnight at 75 percent on the interbank.
O/N money traded between 74.50-75 percent. The average daily overnight rate firmed to 74.85 percent from 70.27 percent Friday.
In the t-bill market, yields firmed before the Treasury's announcement of this week's t-bill auction on cash shortage.
The average yield on the most heavily traded March 12 paper firmed to 124.72 percent from 124.24, Friday's average.
The second most active February 12 paper yielded 122.36 percent after Friday's average of 122.60 percent.
The Treasury will auction 189-day t-bills on Tuesday with a Wednesday value date and when 79.6 trillion lira will be cashed in from maturing t-bills.
